examples.en: The professor is sick, so today's class is cancelled.
I saw the cancellation notice and went to the library.

examples.ko: 결강이 생기면 보강 일정을 알려 줘요.
examples.en: When a class is cancelled, they tell us the make-up schedule.
From a student's point of view, a cancelled class is welcome news.

examples.ko: 이번 학기에는 결강이 두 번이나 있었어요.
examples.en: There were two cancelled classes this semester.
The exam range got smaller because of the cancelled class.

explain: 교수님 사정으로 수업이 열리지 않을 때 써요. 학생이 수업에 안 가는 '결석'과 달라요. 빠진 수업을 나중에 채우는 건 '보강'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Use it when a class is not held because of the instructor. It differs from '결석', which is when a student misses class. Making up the missed class later is called '보강'.

examples.en: We did exercises in time with the teacher's commands.
Please call out the commands loudly.
The sound of commands echoed across the playground.
The commands were so fast that it was hard to keep up.
Commands are short, like 'one, two'.

examples.ko: 구령으로 시작하는 아침 체조 시간이 좋았어요.
examples.en: I liked the morning exercise time that started with commands.

explain: 체육 시간, 군대, 행사에서 여럿이 동작을 맞추려고 외치는 말이에요. '구령을 붙이다', '구령에 맞추다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: These are the calls shouted so that many people move in unison, in PE class, the military or events. Typical combinations are '구령을 붙이다' and '구령에 맞추다'.

examples.en: They take emergency calls at the fire station's control room.

examples.ko: 눈이 많이 와서 상황실이 하루 종일 바빴어요.
examples.en: It snowed a lot, so the control room was busy all day.

examples.ko: 대회 상황실에는 큰 화면이 여러 개 있어요.
examples.en: The competition's control room has several big screens.
I work in a broadcasting company's control room.

examples.ko: 사고 소식을 들은 직원들이 상황실로 모였어요.
examples.en: The staff who heard about the accident gathered in the control room.
I'll explain the current situation from the control room.

explain: '상황실'은 재난이나 큰 행사처럼 여러 일이 한꺼번에 일어날 때 정보를 모아 판단하는 방이에요. '사무실'은 평소 일하는 곳이고 상황실은 비상 때 움직이는 곳이에요. 뉴스에서 '재난안전상황실'처럼 자주 나와요.
explain_en: A 상황실 is a room where information is gathered and decisions are made when many things happen at once, such as a disaster or a big event. A 사무실 is an ordinary workplace, while a 상황실 is active in emergencies. In the news you often see it in terms like 재난안전상황실.

examples.en: The letter will be delivered tomorrow.
I hope my feelings get across well.
The meeting contents were passed on to all employees.
It takes a day for the news to reach people.
The message was not conveyed accurately.
The gift will be delivered safely.

explain: '전달되다'는 물건뿐 아니라 말, 소식, 마음처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것에도 써요. 하는 사람을 말할 때는 '전달하다'를 써요. '~에게 전달되다'처럼 받는 사람 뒤에 '에게'가 와요.
explain_en: 전달되다 works for objects and also for invisible things like words, news and feelings. When you name the person doing it, use 전달하다. The receiver takes 에게, as in '~에게 전달되다'.

dis.h: message or item passed on to someone

p.n: 배달되다 is for goods brought to an address, not for words or messages.

examples.ko: 올해는 지방으로 전출을 희망하는 직원이 많아요.
examples.en: This year many employees want to be transferred to a regional office.
A sudden transfer was decided, so I'm preparing to move.

examples.ko: 이사한 뒤에는 주민센터에서 전출 신고를 해야 해요.
examples.en: After moving, you have to file a move-out report at the community center.

examples.ko: 전출은 본인 뜻과 상관없이 정해질 때도 있어요.
examples.en: A transfer is sometimes decided regardless of your own wishes.
The HR team announced the list of people being transferred today.

examples.ko: 학생 수가 줄어든 이유 중 하나는 다른 도시로의 전출이에요.
examples.en: One reason the number of students fell is families moving out to other cities.

explain: 반대말은 '전입'이에요. 회사나 학교 인사, 주소 이전 신고처럼 공식적인 일에 써요. 일상에서 이사 얘기를 할 때는 '이사 가다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '전입' (moving in). It is used for official matters such as personnel changes at a company or school, or reporting a change of address. In everyday talk about moving house, people say '이사 가다'.

examples.ko: 영어를 잘하는 친구가 저를 위해 통역해요.
examples.en: A friend who speaks English well interprets for me.
I interpreted English into Korean at the meeting.

examples.ko: 말을 바로 통역하는 일이 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: Interpreting speech on the spot isn't easy.

examples.ko: 한국어를 아주 잘하면 통역할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you speak Korean very well, you can interpret.
Don't worry, I'll interpret for you.
I couldn't eat lunch because I was interpreting.

explain: '통역'은 말을 소리로 바로 옮기는 일이고, 글을 옮기는 일은 '번역'이에요. 그래서 회의에서는 '통역', 책이나 문서는 '번역'이라고 해요. 직업 이름은 '통역사'이고, '통역해 주다'를 자주 써요.
explain_en: '통역' is carrying spoken words across languages on the spot, while moving written text is '번역'. So you use '통역' at meetings and '번역' for books and documents. The job is '통역사', and '통역해 주다' (interpret for someone) is common.

examples.en: The teacher's board writing is neat, so it is easy to take notes.

examples.ko: 오늘 수업은 판서가 많아서 손이 아팠어요.
examples.en: There was a lot of board writing in today's class, so my hand hurt.
I took a photo of what was written on the board.
The professor explains only by speaking, without writing on the board.

examples.ko: 요즘은 판서 대신 화면으로 수업하는 학교도 많아요.
examples.en: These days many schools teach with screens instead of the board.
I can't see the board writing well from the back seats.

explain: 선생님이 칠판이나 화이트보드에 쓰는 글씨를 말해요. 학생이 공책에 적는 '필기'와 짝으로 기억하면 좋고, '판서하다'로도 써요.
explain_en: It refers to what a teacher writes on a chalkboard or whiteboard. It is easy to remember as a pair with '필기', which is what students write in their notebooks, and it can also be used as '판서하다'.
